verdict.tagline: Rewind time and shape a moody, story-driven adventure.
for_you_if: you enjoy story-driven adventures with memorable soundtracks
you want the power to rewind time and change decisions

cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight a time-rewinding mechanic that shapes the story-driven adventure and unlocks new dialogue.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as a story-driven adventure centered around a time-rewinding mechanic that allows players to alter decisions and unlock new dialogue options.

citations.review_text:
[h2]Life is Strange is a game I wish I'd played sooner[/h2]

I can't believe I had this game installed on my PS3 for so long, and only finished it yesterday. I wanted to type some thoughts I had.
 
[h3]The Good[/h3]
+ I love the setting of Arcadia Bay. By the end of the game, you really grow an attachment to the town.
+ The art style & art direction is genuinely brilliant and stunning. I've seen glimpses of future games in the franchise, and honestly, I think this first game still has the best art in the entire series, hands down. It's just such a beautiful game.
+ The whole game gives very autumnal vibes, which I love. It's one of the few games I think really nails that specific feeling throughout.
+ Most characters are well-written, especially Max and Chloe. I love their characterization and chemistry with each other.
+ Unlike most choice-based butterfly effect games, I really appreciate how this game is self-aware of the fact it's a video game, and takes advantage of the medium through its core gimmick - rewinding time. There are so many interesting ways the game encourages you to use rewinding. I was initially scared that this would impact the weight of decisions I made, but honestly, far from it. The rewind power can be used to unlock new dialogue options with newly acquired knowledge, which opens up conversations and makes interactions feel more three-dimensional. The writers knew when to put limits on these powers, too, so it never becomes egregious.
+ I wasn't expecting puzzles when playing this game, but on the odd occasion a puzzle was present, I really enjoyed how it made me think to use the rewind gimmick.
+ The story explores various themes and events tastefully and interestingly.
+ The game excels at build-up and payoff a lot of the time. Things that seem small in the moment it happens could balloon into something more important in the future.
+ Acoustic guitar music isn't really my thing personally, but it suits the game brilliantly. The …

Now this is the kind of story-driven game I can get into. There's plenty of dialogue, but the rewind mechanic and actually being able to change your choices makes it feel like you're playing the story, not just reading it. Great atmosphere and soundtrack too. Curious to see where it goes.

★★★★★ (Highly Recommended)

"A game that will take you on a deeply emotional and unforgettable journey, leaving a lasting impression long after you finish it!

My experience in a nutshell:

The ability to manipulate time and change decisions unlocks a multitude of choices and storylines, making every decision you make leave you pondering it again and again.

The story, characters, and overall atmosphere (along with the phenomenal soundtrack) deliver a rare and immersive dramatic experience.

Prepare to experience moments of excitement, sadness, and amazement as you uncover the secrets of the dark city of Arcadia Bay.

A masterpiece of storytelling, and if you enjoy choice-based games and deep psychological drama, this is a must-play at least once in your life."

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a time-rewind mechanic that lets players undo or change their choices and decisions.

citations.review_text: The game is riveting and the time rewind is an exciting option that allows you to see how different responses play out. (Both a good and bad thing for my indecisiveness... XD) I am having a blast playing through with my partner <3

[h2]Time to Turn Back Time[/h2]

[b]After many years, I decided to buy Life is Strange and play it for the second time to refresh my memory and experience the story from a different perspective as an adult.[/b]

My first encounter with the game was back in childhood (yes, not exactly a game for a kid). However, over time, I had already forgotten most of the plot, except for some of my choices, the ending, and the antagonist. Both then and now, I still enjoy the story and the game itself.

[b]The time rewind mechanic and its concept are quite interesting and convenient.[/b] It allows you to change your decisions if you start having second thoughts after making a choice. Something that other games could sometimes use as well.

It was interesting to compare my old and new choices, as well as be surprised by unexpected twists all over again. [b]If you haven't experienced this game yet, perhaps you're missing out on something.[/b]

[i]For the sake of writing this review, I had to rewind time several times.[/i]

It is a beautiful game, both in terms of the story and the art style. It's been long due on the list of games I wanted to play.... and I am so glad I finally got to experience it for the first time. 

The story revolves around a girl when she discovers she has extraordinary abilities, even with those abilities she comes across some very difficult choices, which will make you reconsider your decision. That is exactly what I absolutely loved about this game, you can explore those choices as many times as you want, and sometimes the outcome still won't be according to your expectations. The game places no restrictions on you.

There's a storm coming.... keep your friends close.

claims.claim: Reviewers characterize the gameplay style as a walking simulator with limited character movement and environmental interaction.

citations.review_text:
Interesting concept (reversing time), soundtrack, and characters but the gameplay is extremely boring. It is basically a walking sim. You just walk around and look at things and talk to yourself. It is a very mellow game created for introverts who want to look at things and reflect on their thoughts about those objects. 

You have very little control over your character. She can't jump or perform actions or go where you want her to go. There are invisible walls everywhere disguised as open areas where you think you should go, and when she hits them she says  "I don't want to go here" and turns around. So mostly you are just walking in circles hitting the Y button repeatedly hoping you look at the right things to complete the mission.

Despite all the high praise this game gets, I really dont get it.  Spoilers I guess but I feel like this game was so pointless.  Like the characters were so unlikable except for Warren but even then Max just completely disregards him.  The only good thing about this game is the power that Max has but even then I dont think this game is as good as other TellTale games or choices matter games.
Chloe has to be the dumbest person alive, genuinely.  Why would I ever save her over the town?  Who is choosing that.  The lack of endings in this game really pissed me off.  TWO ENDINGS? ALL OF OUR CHOICES LED TO 2 ENDINGS? Are we serious?  its either this or that?  How boring  and forgettable of a game.

The only redeeming factor of this game is the plot twist with the teacher which I really liked.  Other than that, the gameplay is very lackluster and feels like a walking simulator.  The characters arent good.  Choices DONT matter at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the soundtrack as a standout element that sets the mood and atmosphere of the game.

citations.review_text:
It is rare for a game to stay with me long after the credits roll, but Life is Strange completely pulled that off.

The setting does so much for the experience. Arcadia Bay feels quiet, lived-in, and nostalgic, and the mix of the indie soundtrack with the painted visuals creates an atmosphere that just pulls you right in.

What really makes the story unforgettable, though, are the characters, especially Max and Chloe. Their bond feels deeply real, complicated, and fiercely loyal. Watching their journey unfold gives the whole narrative so much heart, and the emotional weight of their choices hits way harder than I expected. It is a genuinely moving experience that left a lasting mark on me, and it is a story I know I will keep thinking about for a long time.
2026

I played this game on my Xbox and really liked it so I decided to get it on PC as well just for the improved graphics. It looks really good.
There's something about the vibe that’s just so calm and relaxing to play. Honestly, a huge part of that is the music. The soundtrack is peak and sets the perfect mood for this game. For some reason this game gives me this weird, unexplainable nostalgia for something in which I can't quite put my finger on. 
Out of the entire Life is Strange series, this one is easily my favorite.

It is very low stimulation game and the soundtrack are just top-tier. Recommended to play in the middle of the night,in the dark and alone. This game showed me what friendships can be like in certain circumstances

citations.review_text:
It's a neat choose-your-own-adventure style of game, about a girl with time travel powers. It starts out relatively chill, and gets more intense as you go.

I enjoyed the story overall, but I think the endings could've been better. Kind of a bummer to end an otherwise good story on such a downer.

The only other critique I can think of is that the facial animations and lip sync are pretty simplistic. But it's not a big deal. It kind of has its own charm. The remaster supposedly fixes this, but overall I think this original version looks better.

What a great story , The music in this game is so calming and relaxing and the vibes too .
Its a small town mystery game with superpowers where you have the ability to rewind time .
The dialgoues can get cheesy at times and as the game is quite old it has some problems like Lips not syncing well with the dialgoues . 
There is a unexpected plot twist aswell which was very well done . 
Overall a must play if you are looking for a good story with chill gameplay and choices that somewhat matter

The OG, what an amazing story. Lip syncing is quite jarring at points and it has started to show its age as compared to the new Remaster, but it's still peak. Plus it's a lot less buggy than the Remaster.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes a time-rewind mechanic that allows players to experiment with choices and try different solutions.

citations.review_text: Amazing storyline, Max is clearly a very deep character with a lot of potential. The feature of rewinding time adds a brilliant layer to the choices you make, letting you experiment before dealing with the consequences. The storyline between Max and Chloe feels very grounded and real. 10/10, I am so excited to play the next episodes.

Wow, hella bummed I haven't played this earlier but I'm glad I eventually did. The story is engaging, mysterious and at times dark/tragic. It captures the teenage angst in a beautiful manner through Maxs diary, texts to other characters and all the small interactions and thoughts you can discover throughout the game. 

The choices the game faces you with feels impactful and some are detrimental to the story and will stick with you as the game holds you accountable for the actions you've made throughout the story. Some come back multiple episodes later to remind you of your previous actions, adding an extra level of detail that I found myself enjoying, for better or worse.

The rewind ability is the thing that drives the story forwards(/backwards?)and the gameplay elements are mostly straight forward with a handful of exceptions which forces you to really think.

I appreciated the amount of effort and thought that has gone into all the different interactable items, the diary, text messages and characters thoughts from Max perspective. I once again found myself walking around trying to find every single optional photo or optional dialog, all of it helping to paint the bigger picture of the world we've been thrown into.

It's clear this story has taken inspiration from shows like Twin Peaks, not only with the famous "Fire walk with me" which can be found, but also how the story ramps up to its climactic moments in episode 5. 

The soundtrack is beautiful and filled with a melancholy touch and enhances the different story beats and themes, although there were certain scenes where I found myself wanting some music that didn't have any. But maybe that would have taken away from the scenes that actually used music.

The dialog can at times be a bit cheesy and rushed but for the 95% of the game it feels natural and flows seamlessly.

Although the game is fairly old it still holds up in quality, the art style, composition, atmosphere and lighting bringing it all together nic…

Life is Strange is a heartwarming masterpiece.

The story constantly kept me on the edge of distress because I have to make decisions which eventually would lead to different consequences. I'm very indecisive, so to me it was a difficult yet interesting experience. The time rewinding ability is a great addition to the story as well because it requires a certain amount of brain juice. Sometimes you can't just rewind and be there early but have to actually think of a different solution.

The drama and incidents at Arcadia Bay surely made the story whole lot interesting, but as an introvert, having a close friend like Chloe and the ability to social is truly a dream. Chloe might be a troublesome person, but she is also a caring person. She cares Max so much that, if anything happened to Max, she would definitely stand up for her. I wish I had a friend like Chloe. Max's ability to just stomp into anywhere looking into people's stuff is also impressive.

The background soundtracks are also very relaxing and calming. As the plot thickens, it feels like the soundtracks are making the story even more dramatic. Oh, I love the voice actors as well. There are a few of them voicing multiple characters and they speak so well that you can barely tell they are different people's voices.

I don't have real friends nor an interesting life, so to me, playing Life is Strange is like experiencing another life, but a better life despite having degenerated people like (spoiler not provided). You could say I'm playing Life is Strange because my life is not strange enough.

ABSOLUTE PEAK STORY WITH GREAT PLOT TWISTS AND ENDINGS, choices actually does matter so dont fuck up and think over the dialouges and use time rewind as much as possible to follow the best possible path you think is right. 10/10
